prompt_text: Who is the best roofer in Denver for hail damage repair?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: there isn’t one objectively “best” roofer for every Denver hail job — the right contractor depends on your location, roof size/materials, insurance status, and whether you need help with claims. I can help you find or evaluate the best option for your situation. 

How to find the best Denver roofer for hail damage
- Look at recent, local storm-season experience — hail specialists understand insurance processes and storm-driven workload.
- Verify insurance & licensing — company should carry general liability and workers’ comp. Ask for a Certificate of Insurance.
- Check manufacturer certifications — GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, Owens Corning Preferred are good signs.
- Read recent, detailed reviews on Google, Yelp, BBB and Nextdoor; prefer contractors with many recent positive reviews for hail work.
- Ask for local references and photos of completed hail-repair jobs in Denver.
- Get at least 2–3 written estimates that itemize materials, labor, tear-off, permit fees and disposal.
- Confirm warranties — manufacturer shingle warranty and contractor workmanship warranty (written).
- Watch for red flags: door-to-door “storm chasers,” high-pressure sales, demands for full payment up front, offers to sign your insurance check, lack of permits.

Questions to ask any roofer
- Are you licensed/registered to work in Denver? Do you pull permits?  
- Can you provide a current Certificate of Insurance?  
- Do you have manufacturer certifications? Which?  
- Can you give local references and photos of similar hail jobs?  
- Will you help coordinate with my insurance company? How?  
- What is included in the written warranty and length?  
- What is the estimated timeline? How do you handle unexpected issues?  
- Payment schedule and final lien waiver on completion?

Insurance-claim tips for hail damage
- Document damage with clear photos/videos and date-stamp them.  
- Notify your insurer promptly and keep all estimates and communications.  
- You may get the insurer’s adjuster and a roofer’s estimator — don’t sign away rights or accept an assignment-of-benefits without understanding it.  
- A reputable roofer will help prepare supplemental estimates if the insurer misses items.

Typical pricing (very rough)
- Minor repairs: a few hundred to a few thousand dollars.  
- Full shingle roof: often $5k–$20k+ depending on size, steepness, materials, and decking replacement. Exact price varies widely.

Next steps I can help with
- If you share your ZIP code I’ll give instructions for finding top-rated local roofers and review sites to check.  
- If you already have 2–3 estimates, paste them and I’ll help compare line-by-line and flag concerns.  
- If you want, I can draft an email or checklist to send to prospective roofers.

Which would you like to do next?
